Dearest Traveler,

The Seto Inland Sea is a tranquil, maze-like sanctuary of quiet blue waters and sleepy green islands. Here, the sea channels are so calm they resemble a giant lake, mirroring the warm, gentle sun. In recent decades, these sleepy fishing villages have transformed into a world-famous open-air canvas of modern art.

On islands like Naoshima and Teshima, concrete museums designed by master architects emerge from the soil, housing masterpieces that ask us to look closer at the sky, the water, and ourselves. Seto reminds us that even the most forgotten shores can be reborn into magnificent expressions of beauty.

In quiet harmony,
Kokoro of Seto
